observations.finding: The Block 4 T2 verify step includes 'grep -B1 -A1 'entry_flavor="codex"' /tmp/happy-session-recovery.sh.block4' but the actual inserted guard uses '[ "$entry_flavor" = "codex" ]' — the string 'entry_flavor="codex"' does not appear verbatim in the patch text. The grep will return no output, potentially confusing the user into thinking the guard is absent. The adjacent 'grep -c 'entry_flavor=' ...' (also in T2) DOES match correctly and is sufficient for verification. The mismatch grep is advisory-only noise.
observations.recommendation: Replace 'grep -B1 -A1 'entry_flavor="codex"'' with 'grep -B1 -A1 '\"\$entry_flavor\" = \"codex\"'' to match the actual conditional syntax, or remove the -B1 -A1 grep and rely on the 'grep -c 'entry_flavor='' that correctly fires.

observations.finding: Dev-report top-level status is 'completed' but BA ticket AC7 requires status to reflect 'blocked_pending_manual_apply' or equivalent (explicitly forbids 'complete'/'closed'/'闭环' claims). The dev-report does contain 'pending_user_tty' object listing all 5 user-required steps, and SOP document status is 'blocked_pending_manual_apply', so the BA-deliverable-neq-closure stance IS communicated — just not via the top-level status field. This is outside the QA prompt's literal AC8 check but is noted as a documentation inconsistency.
observations.recommendation: Future dev cycles: set top-level dev-report status to 'blocked_pending_manual_apply' when the cycle produces documentation artifacts for user-TTY-only closure steps. The 'completed' status on an SOP-only cycle misleads downstream tooling.
